ranked_evidence.title: $149 For Purell? The Coronavirus Sparked Wild Price Hikes, And Amazon And Others Are Cracking Down.
ranked_evidence.snippet: **Topline**: Hand sanitizers, face masks and rolls of toilet paper—items that weeks ago were seen as mundane—have increased dramatically in value online as sellers try to profit off fears about Covid-19, while some retailers are limiting the number sold per customer to prevent shortages. * Bottles of Purell, among other brands, are going for $149 on eBay, while a 12-pack of Ecofinest hand sanitizer was going for $107 as of Wednesday afternoon. * On eBay, listings for face masks are receiving thousands of views each day, while *Wired* reports that some were being listed on Amazon for up to five times what they were being sold for just weeks ago (one eBay listing for 100 disposable face masks went for $130 as of Wednesday). The World Health Organization has called for governments to boost supply of personal protective equipment, such as face masks, gloves and face shields, by 40% as it warns that health workers on the front lines face shortages.

ranked_evidence.title: Coronavirus: Is it rational to hoard sanitizer and toilet paper? - Los Angeles Times
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Stockpiling sanitizer, toilet paper is understandable. Consumers worldwide have responded to coronavirus fears by stockpiling food, water, hand sanitizer, toilet paper and more. Judy Parra, office manager of the Los Angeles chapter of the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation, called Costco this week about purchasing about a dozen cases of bottled water for an upcoming event. “They said they hoped to have more water in stock the next morning,” Parra recalled. Coronavirus fears have prompted consumers nationwide and around the world to snatch up as much hand sanitizer, toilet paper, cleaning products and other goods as they can cram into a shopping cart. Shelves at many leading retailers are now empty — despite assurances from the business world that most of these products are not in short supply and will be readily available in coming months. “Our choices are influenced by what we think and feel at the moment,” said Ravi Dhar, a marketing professor at Yale University and director of the Center for Customer Insights.
